_comment: Example override file for SUI_LABELS_FILE, or for manage_labels action='import'. Labels attribute addresses so fund tracing is readable and stops at known sinks. Categories cex|bridge|mixer|malicious|burn terminate a trace — a wrong one silently truncates every future trace through that address, so record what you can stand behind and say where it came from. The shipped set (src/data/labeled-addresses.json) deliberately contains almost nothing: this project does not ship attribution it cannot verify.
_sourcing: Two kinds of claim, worth keeping apart. A BEHAVIOURAL claim ('exchange-scale, balanced flow, 400 counterparties measured on 2026-08-08') is derivable from public chain data with get_address_fanout — you can make it yourself and stand behind it. A NAMED claim ('this is Binance') is not derivable from the chain: no measurement distinguishes Binance from Bybit. Named attribution comes from an explorer, an exchange's own disclosure, or a paid data provider — record which, because a reader cannot check it otherwise.
_chains: A bare key is a Sui address and applies on every Sui network. To label an account on another chain — the Ethereum side of a Wormhole exit, say — use a CAIP-10 key: 'eip155:1:0x5aaeb6053f3e94c9b9a09f33669435e7ef1beaed' or 'solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp:<base58>'. Addresses are normalized per chain: EVM keys are lowercased and must be 20 bytes, and Solana keys keep their base58 case.
